title: Legal redlines scratchpad - Mia Wilson
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for negotiating enterprise contract redlines (Dedicated / Private deployments). Mostly shorthand - use for calls with Sales / Solutions / SRE.

Quick checklist - clauses to watch:
- Data ownership & usage: customer insists on ownership of outputs and derivative IP. Watch for overly broad "use" language allowing us to use customer data for model improvement. Propose: no use for model training without explicit opt-in; allow telemetry for performance/ops in aggregate + pseudonymized.
- Confidentiality scope: ensure definition of Confidential Info excludes aggregated/non-identifiable telemetry and general knowledge. Add mutuality and return/destroy obligation on termination.
- Security & breach: require 72-hr notification for confirmed breaches (customer asks 24h - push back). Include obligation to cooperate in remediation and customer-facing comms process. Define indemnity carve-outs.
- Liability / damages cap: typical ask = cap at greater of (fees paid in prior 12 months) or $X. Customer pushing unlimited / high cap for data breach. Negotiation: cap at 12 months fees; carve-out for gross negligence/willful misconduct and for IP infringement (mutual). Consider sub-cap for data breach equal to twice 12-month fees? check with legal.
- Indemnity: push for mutual indemnity; limit to direct damages and associated legal fees. Avoid broad third-party claims that include model outputs unless IP infringement.
- SLA / uptime & service credits: specific measurement windows matter. Customer wants 99.9% for Hosted & Dedicated - confirm whether Dedicated guaranteed in contract or best-effort. Define what counts as downtime (scheduled maintenance excluded, but need clear maintenance window notices and caps). Service credit formula: usually % credit of monthly fees pro rata - push to cap credits at e.g., 50% of monthly fees per month and total per year.
- Termination & transition assistance: customer wants 6 months of free transition/porting. Propose 30 days paid transition at our standard rate; include data export format and assistance SLAs.
- Audit & compliance: limit frequency (once per 12 months) and require mutual NDA for auditors; prefer attestations (SOC2 report) over on-site audit.
- Data residency & encryption/KMS: customer requests strict residency + customer-managed KMS. Confirm product supports customer KMS for Private; for Hosted, propose region locks and bring-your-own-key (if available).
- Subprocessors & subcontractors: require prior notice and ability to object for critical subprocessors.
- Export controls & sanctions: standard compliance language - ensure we block service for sanctioned customers.
- Open source / model licensing: clarify liability for model outputs and any third-party model license conditions. Customer trying to push responsibility for model behavior - push back: we will use commercially reasonable efforts but not guarantee outputs.

Negotiation talking points (for Sales handoff or call):
- We can agree to a reasonable SLA but need to align on how downtime is measured and what counts. Ask: can you share typical traffic patterns and critical windows?
- Data use: we don't train on customer data without opt-in. Offer a paid analytics/benchmarking dataset option if they want model improvement.
- Liability: propose mutual 12-month fee cap. Explain rationale: predictable exposure tied to revenue, limits for startups.
- Audit: provide SOC2 + quarterly transparency report; allow one limited third-party audit per 12 months with reasonable notice.
- KMS/HSM: Private deployments support customer-managed keys. For Hosted, we offer BYOK in limited regions - need to check region.
- Transition: include defined export format (JSONL + metadata), 30 days paid transition assistance, and option to purchase extended migration bundle.

Unresolved / open questions (to chase down):
- Does current Dedicated contract template include BYOK clauses? (Action: ping infra/product)
- SLA baseline: what is realistic for Dedicated under normal load? (Action: ask SRE / Serving-runtime team for empirical 3-month uptime numbers + weekly maintenance windows)
- IP infringement indemnity: do we accept customer unilateral indemnity if they demand? (Action: legal sync)
- Audit frequency acceptable to Product/SRE: once/year plus adhoc in incident?

Draft redline phrases to propose (shorthand):
- "Customer Data" means data provided by Customer. Provider will not use Customer Data to train models or improve models without Customer's prior written consent. Provider may use aggregate, de-identified telemetry for operational improvements.
- "Security Incident" - Provider will notify Customer within 72 hours of confirmed incidents materially affecting Customer Data and will provide remediation updates every 5 business days until resolved.
- "Liability Cap" - Except for liability arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, or indemnity obligations for IP infringement, each party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the amount paid by Customer to Provider under this Agreement in the preceding 12 months.
- "Service Credits" - For downtime measured as total minutes in a monthly measurement period, Provider will issue service credits equal to X% of monthly fees (formula). Total annual credits shall not exceed 50% of a single month's fees.

Practical negotiation strategy / scribbles:
- Start by removing absolute/unlimited liability asks and replace with 12-month cap + carve-outs.
- Trade concessions: if customer wants lower cap, ask for stronger SLAs or longer contract term/commitment.
- For audit requests, offer SOC2 + limited virtual audit; resist on-site if possible.
- If customer insists on BYOK for Hosted, discuss paid Dedicated or Private deployment instead.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
1) Update contract template draft to include 72-hr breach notification and explicit BYOK wording for Private; circulate to Noah (legal) and Olivia (product).
2) Get SRE uptime numbers + definition for downtime. (Assign: Olivia)
3) Prepare fallback redline language for Sales to use (mutual cap, audit frequency, KMS options). (Assign: me)
4) Add clause examples to Confluence page (link above) and link PR for template.

Notes to self / meeting prep:
- In call, keep examples ready: what does a 99.9% SLA mean in minutes? (44 minutes/month). Use that to set expectations.
- Be ready to explain why model outputs cannot be fully indemnified - risk environment.
- Ask whether customer has specific regulatory obligations (HIPAA, GLBA) - if yes, escalate for Private + legal/cert review.

Misc fragments (raw):
- "Customer wants unlimited injunctive relief for data leak" -> ask for narrow injunctive only where appropriate.
- "Escrow?" -> usually only for very large enterprise or for long-term Private/on-prem deals.
- "Maintenance windows: try to lock to Sundays 02:00-06:00 UTC"

End of scratchpad.
_notes: personal scratchpad - informal; keep in Drive for quick access by legal/sales
